protocol.description:
This protocol tells a client where the desktop's text cursor is, so that something meant to act on the text being typed — a character picker, a completion popup — can be put beside it rather than in the middle of the screen.
The position is the one applications report through zwp_text_input_v3.set_cursor_rectangle. It is deliberately the *last* reported caret rather than the current one: a client asking this question has usually just taken the keyboard for itself, at which point the text field it wants to sit beside is no longer the focused one.
Reporting the caret is optional for applications, and many never do — most terminals, and anything running under Xwayland. A client of this protocol must therefore have somewhere sensible to put itself when the answer is "unknown", and must not wait indefinitely for a position.

interface.name: otto_text_cursor_manager_v1
interface.description: The manager global allows clients to ask where the text cursor is.

request.name: get_text_cursor

description.summary: watch the text cursor for a seat

request.description:
Create an object reporting the position of the text cursor on the given seat.
The compositor sends the current state immediately, so a client may create this object and act on the first event it receives without waiting for anything else to happen.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager object. This does not affect text cursor objects already created.

interface.name: otto_text_cursor_v1

description.summary: the position of the text cursor

interface.description:
Reports where the text cursor is, in the layout coordinates the compositor places surfaces in — the same space a fullscreen layer surface covers, so a client anchored to the whole output can use these values directly.
Exactly one of "position" or "unavailable" is sent when the object is created, and again whenever the answer changes.

event.name: position
event.description:
The rectangle the text cursor occupies, in layout coordinates.
The rectangle is the caret itself, not the text field around it: a client placing a panel should sit clear of the whole rectangle so it does not cover the character being typed.
Width or height may be zero for a caret reported as a bare point.

event.name: unavailable

description.summary: the text cursor position is not known

event.description: No application has reported a caret position, or the surface that reported one is gone. A client should fall back to placing itself wherever it would if this protocol did not exist.
